turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so I'll be direct: my son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Why is it on his record before I heard a word from you?
Thanks for coming in. I owe you an apology: the zero went in before I called you.
Okay. That's a start, Hale. Now tell me what you're basing the zero on, because I'm not leaving here with it still in the gradebook.
I am withdrawing the zero today. Owen does a private supervised rewrite at lunch. Nothing goes on his record. I will email you that tonight.
I'm writing that down. If the zero is withdrawn, why does he need a rewrite at all, and what happens to the essay he already handed in? I want the answer to that before I talk about lunch.
Here it is in writing, signed.
Hand it over, I'll read it before I say anything. And Hale, that doesn't answer what I asked: what happens to the essay he already submitted?
Thank you for your time, Ms. Kalinowski.

We're not finished, Hale. I asked what happens to the essay he already handed in, and you haven't answered. I'm reading this page now, and I'll want the withdrawal showing in the gradebook, not only on paper.
I'm still in this chair, Hale. Answer the question about the essay Owen handed in, and then I'll decide whether this page is enough.
